AT A GLANCE
statjam.uk/potus

US Presidential Elections

Results for each election since 1948 with selected statistics

Big figures

59
Presidential elections have taken place since 1788
45

individuals, all men, have been President with Grover Cleveland and Donald Trump the only two Presidents to serve non-consecutive terms having run for President more than twice. Trump is therefore the 44th President and both the 45th individual and the 47th appointment to the role.

24
Presidents served four years or less. The shortest Presidency was held by William Henry Harrison who died only 31 days after taking office.
5
Presidents elected despite losing the popular vote (J.Q. Adams, Hayes, B. Harrison, G.W. Bush and Trump in 2016).
1
President appointed without ever being elected (Ford).
18
Republican Party Presidents
17
Democrat Party Presidents

Results including voteshares alphabetically by state

Figures per state per election are approximate and rounded-UP percentages.

Gerald Ford contested the 1976 election as President having replaced Richard Nixon who resigned. Lyndon Johnson contested the 1964 election as President in place of the assassinated John Kennedy.

State and total of Electoral College votes per year
X

The square area with diagonal lines in each cell represents 12,000,000 people. The red and blue areas within this represent Republican and Democrat votes within the according state as a percentage of 12M. This aims to convey the number of votes each party receives per state proportionally, as a means of highlighting the significant differences in population per state and in turn how and where the Electoral College affects the value of a vote significantly depending on the state it's cast in.

The winning party (R for Republican, D for Democrat; see key above for others) is listed first with their winning percentage of the vote, followed by the runner-up party and their voteshare percentage. Under that the approximate population of the state is listed alongside the turnout (by % of eligible voters where this estimation was already provided online from sources collated by the University of Florida Elections Lab).

About this page

This page was first published in November 2016. Information on this page may change as a result of any inaccuracies identified. Sources of data for this page include Wikipedia, Florida University Election Lab, NBC News (for 2016-2020), the US Election Atlas (est. 1999), United States Election Project and World Population Review.
